description: A ranked set of hypotheses about one primary subject, each carrying a self-reported confidence, plus the actions the diagnosis recommends.

body/hypotheses.label: Hypotheses
body/hypotheses.description: Optional in the declared sense only: an inconclusive diagnosis may carry none, while identified and suspected cannot.

body/hypotheses/*/confidence.label: Confidence
body/hypotheses/*/confidence.description: Pinned to a higher-is-better unit-interval score, which makes minimum, maximum and target forbidden by derivation rather than by decree.

body/actions/*/addresses.label: Addresses
body/actions/*/addresses.description: A leaf, not a container: the grammar cannot address an element of a scalar array, because scalars have no id and positions are not addresses.

go_only_rules.rule: An identified or suspected conclusion requires at least one hypothesis; inconclusive requires none.
Hypothesis ranks must be unique and must cover exactly 1..N for N hypotheses; which hypothesis takes which rank is the producer's judgment.
An identified conclusion requires the rank-1 hypothesis to carry at least one evidence anchor.
Every entry of an action's addresses must name a hypothesis id declared by this same record.
An anchor's subject must name a subject this record declares.

The locator kind decides which locator fields must be present and forbids the rest: file-lines and log-lines require a canonical relative path with a positive start and an end at or after it; byte-range requires a path with a nonnegative start and an end strictly after it; json-pointer requires a valid non-root JSON pointer alone; opaque requires a value alone.
Nothing verifies that an anchor points at anything. Anchor content hashes are deferred, so every locator detail is a producer claim.
